---
title: Announcement banner
---

## Overview

A website can show a short announcement at the top of its pages, inside
the site header: a beta notice, a pointer to release notes, a warning
that some pages are still in progress. Set it once in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
website:
  announcement: "This site is in beta. Expect rough edges."
```

The text is markdown, so emphasis, code and links work:

```yaml
website:
  announcement: "Quarto 2 is out! Read the [release notes](news.qmd)."
```

Links are written relative to the project root, like the other links in
`_quarto.yml`, and resolve to the right URL on every page.

## Options

To change how the banner looks or behaves, use the map form, with the
text under `content`:

```yaml
website:
  announcement:
    content: "Some pages have not been reviewed yet."
    type: warning
    icon: info-circle
    position: below-navbar
    dismissable: true
```

| option | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `content` | markdown text | (required) |
| `type` | `primary`, `secondary`, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info`, `light`, `dark` | `primary` |
| `icon` | a [Bootstrap icon](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/) name, such as `info-circle` or `megaphone` | none |
| `position` | `above-navbar`, `below-navbar` | `above-navbar` |
| `dismissable` | `true`, `false` | `true` |
| `remember-dismissal` | `true`, `false` | `true` |

`type` picks the banner's colors, using the matching Bootstrap alert
style. A site without a navbar still shows the banner at the top of the
page.

## Closing the banner

When `dismissable` is `true` (the default), the banner has a close
button. By default the browser remembers that the reader closed it, and
the banner stays hidden on every page of the site. Changing the
announcement text shows the new announcement again, even to readers who
closed the old one.

To let readers close the banner on the page they are reading without
hiding it everywhere else, set `remember-dismissal: false`. The banner
then comes back on the next page. This suits a notice that applies to
some pages and not others, such as the per-page opt-out below.

With `dismissable: false` the banner has no close button.

## Turning the banner off for some pages

Every page inherits the announcement from `_quarto.yml`. To turn it off
for one page, set it to `false` in that page's front matter:

```yaml
---
title: "Getting started"
website:
  announcement: false
---
```

To turn it off for a whole directory, put the same setting in that
directory's `_metadata.yml`:

```yaml
website:
  announcement: false
```

A page can also change a single option and keep the rest. This page
shows the site's announcement in red:

```yaml
---
title: "Breaking changes"
website:
  announcement:
    type: danger
---
```

## llms.txt

When the site produces [llms.txt](llms-txt.qmd) output, the
announcement is left out of the markdown companions, `llms.txt` and
`llms-full.txt`. It is site chrome, like the navbar and footer, not page
content.

## Differences from Quarto 1

- A page can turn the announcement off, or change its options, in its
  front matter or `_metadata.yml`. Quarto 1 reads the announcement only
  from `_quarto.yml`.
- `remember-dismissal` is new in Quarto 2.
- The close control is a keyboard-accessible button with a label for
  screen readers.
